classification.difficultyReason: Link histogram frequencies to totals and percentages, use cumulative counts to locate the median class, and explain how the upper tail affects the mean relative to the median.

content.prompt: Auction prices of houses sold in Blackpool over the month of September 2016 are shown in the histogram below.

spec.description: Equal-width 50-thousand-dollar intervals, horizontal grid, labelled ticks, and an axis break before 300.
spec.answerVisibility: All bars are permanent source givens.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Determine the total number of houses sold in Blackpool over the month of September 2016.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Determine the percentage of houses, sold in Blackpool over the month of September 2016, that are cheaper than $\$500000$. Give your answer to the nearest whole percent.

answer.worked: Most houses sold at lower prices, with a long tail extending towards the higher prices. The distribution is positively skewed.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Determine the class of prices in which the median occurred.

answer.short:
$\$450000\leq\text{price}<\$500000$.

Locate the 24th ordered price using cumulative frequencies.
answer.worked: There are 47 houses, so the median is the 24th ordered price. The cumulative frequencies are 3, 11, 23 and 32 for the first four classes. The 24th price is therefore in the $\$450000$ to less than $\$500000$ class.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Identify whether the mean or median house price would be greater and explain why.

answer.short: The mean would be greater; the high prices pull it upwards.
answer.worked: The distribution is positively skewed. A few houses sold for much higher prices than most of the others, pulling the mean upwards more than the median. The mean would therefore be greater.
